create_assistant.description: Create a Vapi voice assistant - the agent that answers and places calls. Every field is optional: leave them all empty and Vapi creates one on its own defaults, which you can then shape from the dashboard.

mock_response.firstMessage: Hi, this is Ada calling from the clinic.
mock_response.name: Appointment reminders

create_assistant.name: create_assistant

parameters.description: A name for your own reference, at most 40 characters. Vapi needs one before a call can be transferred between assistants.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What the assistant says as soon as the call connects. Leave empty and it waits for the caller to speak.
parameters.name: first_message

parameters.description: The instructions the assistant follows - who it is, what it is for, what it must not do.
parameters.name: system_prompt

parameters.description: Who supplies the assistant's model. Defaults to openai. Anything other than openai and vapi needs that provider's credentials added in the Vapi dashboard first.
parameters.name: model_provider

parameters.description: Which model to use. Free text rather than a list, because Vapi's model catalogue runs to over 150 entries and retires them on notice. Leave empty to use gpt-4o with openai; every other provider needs one of its own model names.
parameters.name: model_name

parameters.description: How much the model varies its wording, from 0.0 (always the same) to 2.0. Vapi's default is 0.5.
parameters.name: temperature

parameters.description: The longest reply the model may generate in one turn, from 50 to 10000. Vapi's default is 250, which is about a long sentence or two.
parameters.name: max_tokens

parameters.description: Who supplies the assistant's voice. Defaults to vapi, which needs no extra credentials; every other provider has to be connected in the Vapi dashboard first.
parameters.name: voice_provider

parameters.description: Which voice to speak with, as that provider names it. Browse and listen to them under Voice Library in the Vapi dashboard. Required if you choose a voice provider.
parameters.name: voice_id

parameters.description: Whether the assistant opens the call or waits.
parameters.name: first_message_mode

options.label: The assistant speaks first, in its own words
The assistant waits for the caller

parameters.description: Ambience played behind the assistant. Phone calls default to office ambience and web calls to silence.
parameters.name: background_sound

parameters.description: Vapi ends the call once it reaches this many seconds, from 10 to 43200. Defaults to 600.
parameters.name: max_duration_seconds

parameters.description: What the assistant says before it hangs up. Leave empty and it hangs up without saying anything.
parameters.name: end_call_message

parameters.description: What the assistant leaves if the call goes to voicemail. Leave empty and it hangs up.
parameters.name: voicemail_message

parameters.description: Phrases that end the call if the assistant says them, such as 'goodbye'. Case insensitive.
parameters.name: end_call_phrases

parameters.description: Anything of your own to store on the assistant, as an object. Vapi keeps it and hands it back; it is never spoken.
parameters.name: metadata

create_squad.description: Group assistants into a squad so one call can be handed between them. The call starts with the first assistant in the list, so order matters.
create_squad.name: create_squad

parameters.description: A name for the squad, for your own reference.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The assistants in the squad, as a list of ids. The call starts with the first one.
parameters.name: assistant_ids

delete_assistant.description: Delete a Vapi assistant. Vapi answers with the assistant it deleted. It refuses if a squad, a phone number or a call still pins one of the assistant's versions.

query_call_analytics.description: Aggregate your Vapi calls: how many there were, what they cost, how long they ran, broken down by assistant, status or why they ended. Defaults to the last seven days.
query_call_analytics.name: query_call_analytics

parameters.description: Calls, or your subscription's usage. Defaults to calls.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: How to combine the values.
parameters.name: metric

parameters.description: Which value to aggregate. To count calls, choose the 'how many' aggregate over 'Calls (count them by id)'.
parameters.name: column

parameters.description: Split the answer into one row per value of these. Leave empty for a single total.
parameters.name: group_by

parameters.description: The start of the range. Vapi defaults to seven days ago.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The end of the range. Vapi defaults to now.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: Split the range into buckets of this size. Leave empty for one bucket covering the whole range.
parameters.name: step

parameters.description: The zone the buckets are aligned to, as an IANA name such as Europe/London. Vapi defaults to UTC.
parameters.name: timezone_name

column.description: The column it was computed over

metric.description: The aggregate that was asked for

rows.description: One entry per group. Each is keyed by the columns you grouped by plus the aggregate itself, named after the operation and the column - 'countId', 'sumCost'. The keys therefore depend on what was asked for, so they are not described further.
